title: Inner language is in the second universal class
statement: For any data object $d$, if its language $R$ belongs to polynomial time, then the language of strings $w$ for which every bit string $t$ has the property that the encoding of $(w,t)$ does not belong to $d$'s bad language belongs to the second level of the polynomial hierarchy's universal class.
